elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3(d) makes an Affiliate assignee of the Depositor the successor without requiring consent, although post-transaction assumption and delivery requirements apply.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3(a) and (b) automatically recognize a Person into which the Depositor merges or which results from its merger as successor, without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3(c) broadly recognizes any Person succeeding to the Depositor's business, which covers an acquisition of that business.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: A purchaser succeeding to the Depositor's business is recognized under Section 5.3(c), broad enough to cover a sale of substantially all business assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not transfer this Agreement to any successor or assignee without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Although ordinary and affiliate assignments by the Servicer require Issuer consent, Sections 7.6(a)-(c) allow merger, consolidation, and business successors to become Servicer without Issuer consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For assignments subject to the general restriction, the added Issuer consent is expressly qualified as “not to be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: Vendor may never transfer this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause bars the Servicer from assigning to a competitor of the Issuer or Depositor, but Sections 7.6(a)-(c) still permit a competitor to become successor through merger, consolidation, or business succession without being expressly subject to that prohibition.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination, resignation, or similar exit right triggered by a Customer change of control.
elements.evidence: No Customer-change-of-control exit right appears. Section 7.1 permits Servicer resignation only upon a determination that it is legally unable to perform.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3 recognizes merger, consolidation, and business successors of the Depositor without requiring consent.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of a successor assignment.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3 requires deliveries to the Issuer, Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, and Rating Agencies, but does not require written notice to the Servicer.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Sections 7.6(a)-(c) recognize merger, consolidation, and business successors of the Servicer without consent.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of a successor assignment.
elements.evidence: Within fifteen Business Days, the Servicer's successor must deliver an Officer's Certificate and Opinion of Counsel concerning the succession to the Issuer and specified trustees and notify the Rating Agencies, providing written post-transaction notice to the Customer side.

elements.element: Customer's other assignments are permitted if the required consents are obtained.
elements.evidence: The general assignment clause prohibits Depositor assignments “without” the specified consents, thereby permitting them when those consents are obtained.

elements.element: No consent required for a Customer's other assignment may be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Only the Issuer's consent is qualified as not unreasonably withheld; the Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, Certificateholders, and requisite Noteholders remain subject to no reasonableness standard.

elements.element: Vendor's other assignments are permitted if the required consents are obtained.
elements.evidence: Except for specified successor routes, the Servicer may assign if the listed consents are obtained.

elements.element: No consent required for a Vendor's other assignment may be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness qualifier applies only to Issuer consent. The other required trustee, Certificateholder, and Noteholder consents may be withheld without an express reasonableness restriction.

result.reason: The redline gives the Depositor the requested affiliate and successor flexibility and adds qualified Issuer consent and a competitor restriction for Servicer assignments. It nevertheless leaves merger, consolidation, and business-succession routes available to the Servicer without Customer consent or an effective competitor bar. It also fails the fallback because the Depositor need not notify the Servicer of a succession and most required consents remain unqualified. The changes are not minimal to a complete position, including the additional Issuer consent imposed on Depositor assignments, and the rendered text retains an incomplete “The Issuer will” fragment.
